contents.title: An Immersive System for Supporting Sense-able Scholarly Sensemaking
contents.abstract: Scholarly sensemaking, such as in-depth literature reviewing and problem formulation, is essential for research, but it has traditionally been conducted through text-heavy interfaces like Google Docs, RoamResearch, and Zotero. Furthermore, abstract and qualitative scholarly information, such as quotes, claims, and evidence, is difficult to materialize in forms other than text. However, text does not inherently support the perception of abstract properties of information that researchers are particularly interested in (e.g., qualities, connections, fairness). In this demonstration, we present our design exploration of an extended reality (XR) system that enhances the “sense-ability” of immaterial properties of information to enhance scholarly sensemaking. This design proposes instability as a sensemaking affordance within an immersive sensemaking system, enabling users to quickly identify weaknesses in arguments.

contents.title: Demonstration of SafeSpeaker: Voice Obfuscation for Resource-Constrained IoT Devices
contents.abstract:
Embodied voice assistants offer an intuitive and powerful interaction modality, but they also pose significant privacy risks when uploading raw voice recordings to the cloud for processing. These voice recordings contain a wealth of private information beyond
just spoken content, such as acoustic features that can be used to identify and track users. Existing privacy approaches either rely on encryption and cloud-side processing (leaving raw audio exposed in transit and storage) or use voice obfuscation algorithms whose compute and memory demands exceed what microcontroller-class IoT devices can sustain in real time. As a result, the most resource-constrained microphone-enabled devices, which are also among the most numerous, lack any practical voice privacy protection. We present SafeSpeaker, a lightweight voice obfuscation framework
that closes this gap by running entirely on the edge device that captures the audio, breaking the link between user identity and speech before any recording leaves the device. SafeSpeaker uses a time-domain, formant-approximate transformation that avoids the frequency-domain transforms used by prior DSP-based approaches, processing audio nearly 2× faster while matching the identity-obfuscation performance (equal error rate) of state-of-the-art resource-aware methods. We demonstrate the practicality of this design with a real-time prototype on a $3 Arm Cortex-M4 microcontroller that sits between a microphone and an off-the-shelf smart speaker while maintaining the usability to understand and respond to voice commands. By making voice obfuscation feasible at this hardware tier, SafeSpeaker extends on-device voice privacy protections to a substantially larger class of microphone-enabled smart devices.

contents.title: Flashpoint: A Thermally-Charged Arcade Experience
contents.abstract: We present Flashpoint, a multisensory experience realized through a wearable interface and multiplayer AR game. Our demo employs vibrotactile and thermal actuators in a gauntlet form factor, leveraging perceptual mechanisms to deliver thermal-tactile feedback that is spatiotemporally dynamic and contextually rich. This approach accomplishes diverse feedback modalities while reducing standard hardware requirements. Experiencing vibration, impact, heat, cold, and visual stimulation, users draw on the gauntlet interactions and rendering to competitively engage within an AR environment, dueling opponents through thermally-charged attacks. Precise feedback pattern design and real-time responsivity to game events foster immersion and engagement, while the interplay of physical and virtual interactions unifies game actions with sensory stimulation. Flashpoint demonstrates opportunities for accessible multisensory interfaces and applied perception-driven design in future research.

contents.title: TurnReel: In-Situ Storytelling with Extended Reality and Video Generation Models
contents.abstract: We present TurnReel, an in-situ storytelling system that transforms a static image into an evolving video narrative. Participants contribute events to a shared canvas by pairing a text prompt with a hand-drawn path or lasso: paths specify movement, while lassos select regions for in-place events. These embodied prompts condition a generative video model that turns each contribution into a short clip, whose final frame becomes the canvas for the next take. Through successive contributions, participants build a shared narrative as a timeline of clips that can later be exported. TurnReel supports asynchronous public participation through both an extended reality interface, enabling embodied interaction with a life-size canvas, and a web interface for remote users. At UIST, attendees will co-create with TurnReel and watch a collective story unfold on site.

contents.title: Demonstrating Kneadix: A Multi-Process Loom with Dynamic Warp-Weft Role Assignment
contents.abstract: Current weaving technology permanently sets the role of the warp and weft yarns during the setup phase of production. This limitation is inherent to the structure of modern looms in which the warp actuation mechanism (heddle) commits the layout before fabrication starts. In this demonstration, we propose a heddle-less loom architecture in which yarn carriers are manipulated by a set of horn gears. By re-interpreting weaving, knitting, and braiding as yarn-twisting processes, we demonstrate that our design can create fabrics combining these processes without seams. We present a proof-of-concept implementation illustrating actuation, yarn tension management, and combing. We used this implementation to validate our design by fabricating fabrics that combine all three processes, manage yarn insertion, and handle complex edge management.

contents.title: Demonstrating Fold2Unfold: Screen Privacy Protection against Shoulder Surfing using Inter-Screen Reflection on Foldable Smartphones
contents.abstract: Smartphone use in crowded public spaces exposes users to shoulder surfing, allowing nearby bystanders to easily access privacy-sensitive information displayed on the screen. We demonstrate our full paper Fold2Unfold, a screen privacy protection system for foldable smartphones that ensures screen content readable only from the user's viewpoint without additional hardware. Fold2Unfold decomposes the original content into two complementary, individually illegible shares displayed across screens, and leverages inter-screen reflection to reconstruct the content. By tracking the user's eye position and dynamically warping the content accordingly, the system ensures that the reconstructed content is readable only to the user.

contents.title: Gaze-Contingent Dual Animation with High-Speed Projection
contents.abstract:
We demonstrate a dual animation display system that simultaneously embeds two independently designed animations in a single high-speed projected display. During free viewing, viewers perceive one animation; when they smoothly track a character or object
moving within the scene, a second animation emerges. This effect requires neither cameras nor sensors, and no deliberate physical interaction is needed. Attendees can experience this gaze-contingent perceptual switching firsthand through multiple video applications.

contents.title: See Through With The Hands: Seamless Occluded Interactions in Augmented Reality
contents.abstract: Augmented Reality (AR) offers the ability to overlay images onto real-world views. See-through views have been explored for spatial understanding in larger scenes, such as through drone-mounted cameras. In this paper, we propose a wrist-mounted device that constructs real-time see-through views for occluded manual interaction without requiring external tracking. The depth image from the camera is transposed to align with the headset view, enabling intuitive body positioning during object manipulation. We combine this with a custom actuated mount that adapts the depth camera's angle to different hand poses. We show that our prototype, despite its simplicity, enables fine manipulation tasks such as aiming at and screwing an occluded nut.

contents.title: Demonstrating Preemptive Physical Feedback Strategies for Sequential Skill Learning: Fingers, Arms, and Heads
contents.abstract:
We invite attendees to experience preemptive physical feedback, that is physical intervention delivered before a motor error is committed, across three body loci and two task scales. The demonstration brings together two systems from our sequential skill augmentation program. 
FIXical I/O (CHI 2026) intervenes at the finger during a micro-scale key sequence, sensing an erroneous finger action and physically correcting it before completion. 
ProtoCall (UIST 2026) intervenes at the arm and at the head during a macro-scale object selection task, aborting an erroneous reach and redirecting attention toward the correct target before the error occurs. By moving from fingers to arms to heads, attendees feel how the body locus and the timing of physical feedback shape guidance, agency, and skill formation in sequential tasks.

contents.title: Demonstration of InvisiSpeech: Making Silent Speech Invisible through a Miniature Intraoral Sensor
contents.abstract:
Silent speech promises private interaction, but existing implementations often rely on visible sensors or conspicuous articulation, which limits their discretion in daily use.
We present InvisiSpeech, an intraoral interface that remains hidden from outside view and supports silent speech input with minimal lip movement and without drawing visual attention. Our custom flex-PCB device is housed in a biocompatible SLA-printed dental brace and attaches around the back molar. This mount couples a voice-pickup sensor to the tooth for input sensing, which our embedded microcontroller transfers via Bluetooth.

contents.title: Demonstration of GuitarFins: Triggering Input with a Guitar Pick
contents.abstract: Controlling digital interfaces (e.g., navigating in a tablature interface via mouse and keyboard) or configuring physical audio equipment (e.g., on the floor) can be challenging with a guitar strapped on, as it impedes physical access to the input devices. In addition, guitarists typically use a guitar pick, which can be a hindrance when trying to interact with physical input components that are not designed around the fact that the index finger and thumb are occupied by the pick. We demonstrate GuitarFins, which turn the guitar pick from a hindrance into an opportunity. GuitarFins are physical input components that are integrated into the guitar corpus and designed to be operated with a guitar pick, thereby utilizing the skill and dexterity of guitarists with a pick.

contents.title: Demo: Weight Exercise Monitoring with a Magnetometer
contents.abstract: Exercise monitoring systems on commercial-off-the-shelf smartphones and smartwatches often rely on the motion of the devices to detect exercises. This leaves a substantial sensing blind spot when the device remains stationary during exercise. We demonstrate ProxiFit, a weight exercise monitoring system that overcomes this limitation with magnetometers built into smart devices. By sensing magnetic field disturbances from ferrous exercise weights, the system can classify and count weight exercises even when the device stays still. This enables previously undetectable scenarios: smartwatches can detect lower-body weight exercises and single-arm exercises performed on the non-watch arm, and smartphones mounted away from the body and the exercise equipment can detect nearby weight exercises.

contents.title: Demonstrating Roomify: Spatially-Grounded Style Transformation for Immersive Virtual Environments
contents.abstract: We present a live demonstration of Roomify, a spatially-grounded transformation system that turns a physical room into themed immersive virtual environments while preserving its layout, furniture locations, and functional semantics. Visitors wear a VR headset, enter a compact room-scale setup, and experience real tables, chairs, boundaries, and small props as stylized virtual counterparts: they can walk, touch furniture, sit down, and switch between six prepared themes, each combining aligned 3D assets, surface materials, lighting, an animated skybox, and matching ambient sound. When booth traffic allows, visitors can also prompt the generative pipeline to create a new themed variation of the same room on the spot. Roomify was published as a full paper at CHI 2026, where two user studies showed significant gains in presence over passthrough and fully virtual baselines while maintaining spatial awareness. The demo makes this result directly tangible: an immersive world that visitors can not only see, but also physically inhabit.

contents.title: Embodied-AI: Providing Users with Physical Assistance by Constraining Multimodal-AI with Embodied Knowledge
contents.abstract: Electrical-muscle-stimulation (EMS) can support physical-assistance (e.g., shaking a spray-can before painting). However, EMS-assistance is highly-specialized because it is (1) fixed (e.g., one program for shaking spray-cans, another for opening windows); and (2) non-contextual (e.g., a spray-can for cooking dispenses cooking-oil, not paint—shaking it is unnecessary). Instead, we explore a different approach where muscle-stimulation instructions are generated considering the user’s context (e.g., pose, location, surroundings). The resulting system is more general—enabling unprecedented EMS-interactions (e.g., opening a pill-bottle) yet also replicating existing systems (e.g., Affordance++) without task-specific programming. It uses computer-vision/large-language-models to generate EMS-instructions, constraining these to a muscle-stimulation knowledge-base & joint-limits. We believe our concept marks a shift toward more general-purpose EMS-interfaces.

contents.title: GlassTENG: Physiological Sensing via Triboelectric Nanogenerators in Smart Glasses
contents.abstract: Smart glasses maintain near-continuous skin contact at multiple arterial and muscular sites, making them a promising platform for physiological sensing. In practice, though, two factors make sustained daily wear and longitudinal deployment impractical for the quantified self: the discomfort of prolonged sensor–skin contact (e.g., gels and adhesives) and the sensor power demands that increase battery size, weight, and maintenance burden. We present GlassTENG, an ultra-low-power sensor that embeds three custom-fabricated triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs) into a glasses frame at the angular artery on the nasal bridge, the superficial temporal artery on an extended arm, and the temporalis muscle at the temple. Each GlassTENG sensor is self-powered in transducing mechanical energy to electrical energy and consumes 1.36μW per sensor at the analog front-end. GlassTENG enables simultaneous capture of arterial pulse waveforms, jaw kinematics (e.g., clenching, tapping, eating), and upper facial activity (e.g., blinking, eyebrow movement). In a 20-participant user study, we achieve 93.8% accuracy across six jaw and upper facial activities and estimate heart rate with a mean absolute error of 1.82 beats per minute (BPM) relative to a ground-truth chest-strap sensor in 30s windows. Together, these results establish a future pathway toward a longitudinally worn, ultra-low-power, glasses-based physiological monitoring platform.

contents.title: Taste as Form: Real-time Crossmodal Visualization of Eating Experiences in Mixed Reality
contents.abstract: We present Taste as Form, a mixed reality system that turns vision-inferred food attributes and real-time chewing dynamics into generative visual structures. The system uses passthrough image analysis to infer a sensory profile of the food, including likely taste category, texture (mouthfeel), and color, synchronized with sEMG sensing of chewing dynamics. Inferred taste cues inform geometric form and color palettes, while texture cues shape material physics and motion behavior. The user's chewing rhythm modulates the onset, intensity, and decay of the visual effects. This work proposes a framework for structuring inferred sensory qualities and mastication as coupled interaction signals for immersive dining and sensory-awareness experiences.

contents.title: Electroluminescent Display Fabrication: Exploring Freedom of Form, Non-Specialist Design and High-Resolution Visual Outputs
contents.abstract: We present a set of demonstrations spanning methods for the personal fabrication of free-form electroluminescent displays. Free-form interactive devices promise interaction capabilities that leverage spatial understanding and object recognition. However, a reliance on fixed-form display components, such as rigid rectangular arrays and encased LEDS, represents the greatest challenge to prototyping and producing interactive devices with custom shapes. Creating such artefacts for further research, personal use and prototyping is limited by current manufacturing pipelines. Electroluminescent (EL) materials can be manipulated in ambient air opening the door to personal fabrication of custom displays. We present demonstrations from three full projects that have contributed to expanding the interactive devices that can be produced through EL fabrication. We include previously not demonstrated applications and technical demonstrations from ProtoSpray (CHI 2020), Dispray (CHI 2026) and Spray and Etch (UIST 2026). Together, these demonstrations showcase the progression of EL display fabrication through integration with 3D printing, exploration of non-specialist use and testing the potential for comparable resolution to commercial devices.

contents.title: Demonstration of TherMosaic: Accelerating Perceived Thermal Transitions Through Spatiotemporal Thermal Feedback
contents.abstract: TherMosaic [12] is a spatiotemporal thermal feedback technique that accelerates perceived temperature transitions by approximately 30%–40% for transitions originating from hot or cold states. In this demonstration, we present a standalone wearable implementation of TherMosaic featuring a custom 2 × 2 array of independently controlled Peltier modules. Through a virtual reality experience, participants will encounter multiple hot-to-cold and cold-to-hot transitions, demonstrating how our approach reduces perceived thermal lag and more closely synchronizes thermal feedback with visual events during interactive use.

contents.title: MagDesk: Demonstration of an Interactive Tabletop Workspace based on Passive Magnetic Tracking
contents.abstract: Accurate and responsive 3D tracking enables interactive and context-aware workspaces, including mixed-reality 3D interfaces and collaborative tangible interactions. However, limitations of current tracking mechanisms—line-of-sight occlusion, drifting errors, small working volumes, or instrumentation that requires maintenance—ultimately restrict their adoption. This demonstration introduces MagDesk, an interactive tabletop workspace capable of real-time 3D tracking of passive magnets embedded in objects. Using a sensing array of 112 low-cost magnetometers underneath a table, our custom-designed signal-processing and localization engine enables simultaneous tracking of multiple magnets in 5 degrees of freedom with millimeter accuracy. MagDesk can continuously and robustly track magnets at a maximum height of 600 mm over a 1750 mm (L) × 950 mm (W) table, while achieving average positional and orientational errors of 2.49 mm and 0.72 deg near the table surface, and 14.40 mm and 2.25 deg across the entire sensing range. To illustrate MagDesk’s object-tracking capabilities, this demonstration presents a series of magnetic widgets for tangible interactions and explores two applications—a 3D drawing interface and augmented-reality tabletop games. By instrumenting a regular table surface, MagDesk presents a low-cost and accurate approach to 3D tracking of passive objects for home and office environments.

contents.title: NodeBots: Physicalizing Network-Based Data with SwarmUIs
contents.abstract: Data Physicalization is an emerging area of data representation that uses a wide variety of physical mediums and data sources. We propose ‘NodeBots’, a novel approach that integrates Swarm User Interfaces (SwarmUIs) with Network Visualizations to create an interactive, swarm-based physicalization of network graphs. NodeBots allows users to physically interact with the nodes of network graphs, creating physical metaphors for embodied graph interactions through the rich affordances of SwarmUIs. In this paper, we explore NodeBots' interaction space and its applied interactions, such as sparse cuts and shortest paths.

contents.title: Demonstration of General Accessibility Models: Learning Accessibility Needs from Everyday Computer Use
contents.abstract: Accessibility research has long envisioned systems that adapt to users' abilities and contexts. Yet current ability-based systems lack reliable ways to learn users' accessibility needs in situ, leaving many individualized and context-specific barriers unaddressed. We present the General Accessibility Model (GAM), an architecture that learns users' accessibility needs by observing everyday computer use. From screen recordings and input streams, GAM generates confidence-weighted propositions describing a user's interaction strategies and in-situ accessibility barriers. Because prolonged interactions are necessary to understand user needs, GAM employs efficient segmentation and context compression, periodically reflecting on observations to revise propositions. We demonstrate how GAM can enable accessibility applications, including accessibility report generation, feature recommendation, and just-in-time accessibility repair. GAM illustrates how everyday interaction can become a source of continuously updated knowledge for personalized accessibility support.
